import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Normality of Irrational Algebraic Numbers

It is unknown whether every irrational algebraic real number is normal in any integer base.
The stronger conjecture that every irrational algebraic real number is absolutely normal is stated
separately: normality in one base and normality in every base are not equivalent definitions.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Normal number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)
- [BC01] Bailey, David H., and Richard E. Crandall. "On the random character of fundamental constant
  expansions." Experimental Mathematics 10.2 (2001): 175-190.
  https://projecteuclid.org/journals/experimental-mathematics/volume-10/issue-2/On-the-random-character-of-fundamental-constant-expansions/em/999188630.full
-/

open NormalNumber

namespace AlgebraicNormality

/-- A real number is irrational algebraic if it is algebraic over `ℚ` but not rational. -/
def IsIrrationalAlgebraic (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsAlgebraic ℚ x ∧ Irrational x

/-- The strong normality conjecture: every irrational algebraic real is absolutely normal. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 12 41]
theorem irrational_algebraic_absolutely_normal :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ x : ℝ, IsIrrationalAlgebraic x → IsAbsolutelyNormal x := by
  sorry

/-- The weaker normality conjecture: every irrational algebraic real is normal in at least one
integer base `b ≥ 2`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 12 41]
theorem irrational_algebraic_normal_in_some_base :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ x : ℝ, IsIrrationalAlgebraic x → ∃ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b ∧ IsNormalInBase b x := by
  sorry

/-- Absolute normality implies normality in at least one base. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem normal_in_some_base_of_absolutely_normal {x : ℝ} (hx : IsAbsolutelyNormal x) :
    ∃ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b ∧ IsNormalInBase b x :=
  ⟨2, le_rfl, hx 2 le_rfl⟩

end AlgebraicNormality

findings.description: The conclusion at line 52 asks only for simple normality in some base, not normality. The imported `NormalNumber.IsNormalInBase` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/NumberTheory/NormalNumber.lean:63–69) counts individual digits `d < b` and requires frequency `1/b`; it never quantifies over longer strings. The existential base quantifier does not supply the missing conditions for all powers of that base. As a definition-level check, /workspace/review/counterexample.lean proves `IsNormalInBase 2 (1/3 : ℝ)`, although the binary block `00` has frequency zero rather than 1/4. This rational example distinguishes the predicates; it is not a counterexample to the irrational-algebraic conjecture.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number, distinguishes simple normality (each digit has frequency 1/b) from normality (every length-k string has frequency b^(-k)). It states the conjecture that every irrational algebraic number is absolutely normal and notes that no such number is known to be normal in any base. Bailey–Crandall [BC01], §2, Definition 2.1, likewise requires 'every finite string of k digits' to have limiting frequency b^(-k); read in the authors' copy at https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/baicran.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the shared definition to require all finite digit-block frequencies. Alternatively, rename the current predicate `IsSimplyNormalInBase` and define full normality by simple normality in every positive power of the base. A minimal correction using the existing definitions is to replace the existential's `IsNormalInBase b x` with `∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → IsNormalInBase (b ^ k) x`.

reformulations.difference: Unfolding the imported `IsAbsolutelyNormal` gives simple normality in every integer base ≥ 2, whereas the source requires full normality in every such base.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Wikipedia's Properties section explicitly states that normality in base b is equivalent to simple normality in every base b^k, k > 0, and hence that absolute normality is equivalent to simple normality in every base. For each b ≥ 2, all b^k are among Lean's quantified bases; conversely, take k = 1. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, `algebraic_absolute_equiv` proves the biconditional with full normality represented by this source-given base-powers characterization. The block-frequency/base-powers characterization itself was cited, not reproved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The displayed conclusion uses the single-digit predicate, so it literally supplies simple normality in some base rather than full normality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under this theorem's `hx : IsAbsolutelyNormal x`, the stronger intended conclusion follows too: choose base 2, and apply hx to 2^k for every k > 0. The source's base-powers characterization then gives full binary normality. Thus, under the stated hypothesis, the two existential conclusions are equivalent. This biconditional was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean using the base-powers characterization as the definition of full normality.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number — definitions, algebraic-number conjecture/status, non-normal numbers, equivalent characterizations, and notes.

Bailey, D. H., and Crandall, R. E., On the Random Character of Fundamental Constant Expansions [BC01], author-hosted preprint dated 3 October 2000: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/baicran.pdf — §§1–2, related discussion in §3, and §7.

review.notes: Checked all four declarations. `IsIrrationalAlgebraic` has the intended meaning; Lean tests exclude rational inputs and establish √2 as a witness. Bases 0 and 1 give degenerate predicates but are excluded by the statements. The n=0 division affects only one term of the limiting frequency, and the fractional-part/natural-floor convention behaves correctly on negative inputs. Both answer slots have the appropriate proposition type and quantifier scope. Wikipedia still records the normality questions as open. The cited Project Euclid page returned an access challenge, so BC01 was read from the author's site. Both scratch files compile; the equivalence and counterexample lemmas have no sorry dependencies. No repository files were edited.

submission.summary: Changed the chosen-base condition to require simple normality in every positive power of that base, which is equivalent to full normality. Updated the theorem’s docstring to explain this characterization; all other declarations remain unchanged. The required Lean compile command succeeds with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
